gaps.sentence: I'd rather you ___ smoke in here.
gaps.explanation: would rather + somebody + past simple: I'd rather you didn't smoke.
would rather takes the bare infinitive: I'd rather stay.

gaps.sentence: He continued ___ as if nothing had happened.
gaps.explanation: continue takes -ing or to-infinitive. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: It's not worth ___ about the delay — nothing will change.
The children are looking forward to ___ Father Christmas.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: looking forward to meeting.

gaps.sentence: The hotel offered ___ our room free of charge.
gaps.explanation: offer takes the to-infinitive: offered to upgrade.

gaps.sentence: He went on ___ even after the audience had left.
gaps.explanation: go on + -ing = continue the same activity; go on to do = do something next.

gaps.sentence: They made me ___ for the whole team's mistake.
gaps.explanation: make + object + bare infinitive in active sentences: made me apologise.
